summary.text: Timothy M. Kennedy is the Democratic incumbent for New York's 26th District, seeking a first full term after winning an April 2024 special election. A Buffalo native and licensed occupational therapist, he served on the Erie County legislature and in the New York State Senate before entering Congress. He sits on the Homeland Security and Veterans' Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Kennedy was born in Buffalo, New York, in 1976. According to his congressional biography, he grew up in a blue-collar Buffalo family with four siblings and attended St. Joseph's Collegiate Institute. He earned bachelor's and master's degrees in occupational therapy from D'Youville College, now D'Youville University, in 1999.
He worked for 11 years as a licensed occupational therapist with geriatric and pediatric patients before entering public office.

Kennedy served on the Erie County legislature from 2004 to 2010. In 2010, he defeated incumbent Democratic State Senator William Stachowski in the primary and then Republican Jack Quinn in the general election for New York State Senate District 58, and he served in the State Senate from 2011 to 2024.

In the State Senate he chaired the Transportation Committee, according to his congressional biography, which says he worked on funding for the Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority's Metro Rail, school bus and work-zone safety legislation, and limousine safety reforms.

Kennedy was elected to the U.S. House in a special election on April 30, 2024. He sits on the Homeland Security Committee, with seats on its Emergency Management and Technology and Transportation and Maritime Security subcommittees, and on the Veterans' Affairs Committee. He co-chairs the Northern Border Caucus and introduced the SNOW Act on FEMA's response to winter weather events, according to his congressional biography.
Kennedy lives in the City of Buffalo with his wife, Katie, and their three children, according to the same biography.
